advisory.name: Ms. Wardak
bio: Miriam Wardak joined Interos in February of 2020 as Senior Vice President, Human Resources to establish the company’s talent framework for a sustainable scale-up operation. Wardak is a talent focused executive with experience in leading Human Resources teams in public and private sectors to deliver results, optimize organizational performance and maximize engagement. Wardak joins Interos as a proven leader in building start-ups, enabling growth within pre-IPO, post-IPO and Fortune 500 companies. Most recently Wardak was leading the People’s Operation function at Repairify Inc. a hyper-growth company located in Plano, Texas. Prior to this, at Project HOPE, a global health development organization, Wardak was responsible for Finance, IT, Human Resources and Facilities operations. Prior leadership roles included the head of HR role at ICF International, a Washington DC-based government consulting organization with over $500M in annual revenue and as Senior Vice President of Human Resources at i2 Technologies, a supply chain software company in Dallas, Texas. Miriam was born in Kabul, Afghanistan, grew up in Germany, and has been living in the United States since 1990. She is fluent in German and Farsi and conversational in Italian and French. Miriam holds a B.A. from George Mason University and an M.B.A. from the University of Dallas.

advisory.name: Dr. Shreeranjan
bio: Dr Shreeranjan had long and distinguished career of 32 years in the Indian Administrative Service and held key positions of responsibility and leadership in various departments and Ministries in both the State Government and Government of India. He was also Joint Secretary for 5 years in the Ministry of Woman and Child Development and was responsible for policy formulation and implementation of government programmes pertaining to child development and child rights, nutrition, early childhood care and education, women empowerment, international cooperation, etc. He also served for about 2 years as Joint Secretary and Additional Secretary to the Govt. of India as Deputy Director General (DDG) in the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), and was also empanelled as Secretary to Government of India. He also served as Chairman, Board of Revenue and Additional Chief Secretary in Government of Meghalaya, and also as Chairman of Meghalaya Biodiversity Board. He has also participated in several prestigious international and national conferences, representing the Country in international forums relating to women and child development and was also awarded National E-Governance Award in 2014.

advisory.name: Dr. Sharad Onta
bio: Present position Dr. Sharad Onta, a medical graduate (MD) in 1984 from Leningrad – former Soviet Union (USSR), has master degree in public health (MPH) from UK in 1992. He completed Ph D in 1999 from Copenhagen, Denmark in health system research. Retired faculty of Tribhuvan University, Nepal He is founding General Secretary of Nepal Public Health Foundation (NPHF). Chair, Resource Centre for Primary Health Care, an NGO President, Physicians for Social Responsibility Nepal (PSRN) Country Coordinator, People’s Health Movement, Nepal Previous positions Dr. Onta was Professor and Head of the Department of Community Medicine and Public Health of Institute of Medicine, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu. His responsibilities included teaching International Health to MPH students, supervising public health master and Ph D students. He was a Member of Academic Council of Tribhuvan University, Member of Academic Council of National Academy of Medical Sciences (NAMS) and Patan Academy of Health Sciences (PAHS). Dr. Onta worked as Executive Director of a National NGO – Resource Centre for Primary Health Care during 1992-1994. In 2007, he was nominated by the Government of Nepal as Executive Member Secretary of Nepal Health Research Council, an authority to approve and monitor health research activities in Nepal. He was also nominated by the Government of Nepal as Executive Chief of HIV/AIDS and STI Control Board in 2009. He was a member of High Level Policy Advisory Body at the Ministry of Health and Population (2007-209). Dr. Onta served as a Senator of BP Memorial Institute of Health Sciences, a Deemed University under the Ministry of Health and Population during 2007-2009. Dr. Onta was Assistant Dean (Academic) of the Institute of Medicine, responsible for academic activities of the institute from 2012 to 2016. Health policy He is extensively involved in development of national health policies, planning and strategies. Dr. Onta contributed to development of national compact for International Health Partnership (IHP). His contribution has been remarkable in development of National Action Plan of HIV AIDS, implement Framework Convention of Tobacco Control (FCTC) in the country, formulate strategy of revitalization of primary health care, develop and implement public health education. He worked as a member of High Level Health Policy Development Committee (2017), formed by Council of Ministers for development of a new National Health Policy in the context of federalization of the country. His particular interest is in health finance system to address equity in health. Networking He has a wide links with several regional and international networks and has experiences of working in other countries. His involvement in People’s Health Movement at the regional and global level has visibly added voice to strategize social determinants of health. Dr. Onta is among the activist physicians to advocate for “peace through health”, as an International Councillor of Physicians for Social Responsibility, Nepal (PSRN), an affiliate to International Physicians for Prevention of Nuclear War (IPPNW). He is an active member of People’s Health Movement, Nepal Chapter to advocate in health right issues. Publications Dr. Onta has published several research articles in national and international journals, produced several reports and contributed to chapters of several books.

advisory.name: Linda Heitzman
bio: Linda is known as a creative, strategic leader who leverages her personal and professional experiences to build lasting relationships, solve tough problems and to identify and seize strategic opportunities. She has a long history of providing strategic advice to support profitable growth through market expansion and organizational effectiveness. Linda has advised a wide range of organizations from Fortune 50 life science and healthcare companies to an international non-governmental global health organization. Linda recently retired from Project HOPE where she served as the Executive Vice President of Global Health. Prior to joining Project HOPE, she held senior positions at both Deloitte Consulting LLP and Ernst & Young Management Consulting after beginning her career in public service. Bertzman Social Ventures is the realization of Linda’s dream to leverage her professional experience and personal passion to make the world a better place.

team.name: Ajay Pal
bio: Ajay Pal, State Program Manager of Karnataka state has over 17 years of experience in project management, planning, implementation, monitoring and field level support to NGO’s. He has worked on public health programs with National and International development agencies in the state of Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana, with focus on HIV/AIDS Prevention, Care and Support programs working with key population. He has managed Tsunami and flood relief programs. He holds M.Phil. in Psychiatric Social Work from NIMHANS, Bangalore and Masters in Social Work (Medical &. Psychiatry) from Loyola College, University of Madras

team.name: Cheena Malhotra
bio: Ms. Malhotra is a passionate public health professional with 18+ years international experience as a senior professional in public health working in both the private and public sectors. Ms. Malhotra has extensive experience in advocacy, policy reform and health systems strengthening with a particular focus on expanding access to healthcare services in India and abroad. Ms. Malhotra’s work across the globe including India, Bangladesh, Suriname, Mexico, Dubai, South Sudan is focused on non communicable diseases, nutrition, WASH, Solid Waste management and rare diseases has resulted in increased state funding for NCDs, the development of NCD training manuals for CHWs, Medical Officers and Para Medicals, monitoring of vaccination programs and key improvements in the national Rare Disease Policy. Ms Malhotra is a post graduate and certified diabetes educator and lactation consultant. She has completed South East Asia regional course on public health by AIIMS Delhi and PGI Chandigarh. She has also completed her fellowship in global policy, diplomacy and sustainability.

team.name: Dr Nalini Kaushik
bio: Dr Nalini is a seasoned public health expert with over 14 years of specialized experience in the pharmaceutical and medical device sectors, delivering services in health policy research, advocacy, regulatory & government affairs, and strategic communications. She has provided strategic guidance to a diverse array of prestigious clients, including WHO-SEARO, ICMR, USAID, Sanofi, ADVAMED, Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Takeda, DSM, Abbott etc. With her keen passion for women and child health she has extensively worked on subjects such as menstrual health, family planning, adolescent health and menopause. So far, she has trained 2000+ individuals, conducted several M&E studies and has curated India's first menopause policy discourse titled "Menopause Dialogue". Dr Kaushik has foundational training in Dental Surgery; and later she received a Masters in Public Policy from National Law School of India University. She also holds a diploma in Global Health Diplomacy from University of Toronto and a Diploma in Menstrual Health and Wellness.

team.name: Mr. Alok Chandra Mohanty
bio: Alok Chandra Mohanty is a social, development and health sector professional having more than 30 years of working experience in various fields and operational areas. He possesses a rich profile of leading a number of large-scale projects being implemented and supported by the Government, International Agencies and Development Partners such as National Health Mission (NHM), United Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children’s Funds (UNICEF), etc. His areas of expertise range from systems strengthening, partnership building, policy advocacy, program implementation, capacity building to resource mobilization and project management. He has demonstrated ability in delivering results within timeline and significantly contributed in project expansion and scaling up in many occasions. He is a team player and has successfully handled large workforces effectively.
